notes: The Argentine Republic, commonly known as Argentina, is a large country in the southern part of South America. It is a federal republic known for its vast plains (Pampas), Andes mountains, and rich cultural heritage, influenced by European immigration. Its geography varies from fertile plains to the Andes mountains and Patagonia. The climate ranges from subtropical in the north to subpolar in the south. Argentina has a significant cultural output in literature, music, and film. Aliases: Argentine Republic.

The Commonwealth of Australia is a sovereign country comprising the mainland of the Australian continent, the island of Tasmania, and numerous smaller islands. Australia is a constitutional monarchy and a federation. It is known for its unique wildlife, diverse landscapes ranging from deserts to rainforests, and its distinct cultural identity. The climate varies significantly across the continent, from tropical in the north to temperate in the south. Aliases: Commonwealth of Australia.

The Republic of Austria is a landlocked country in Central Europe, characterized by its mountainous terrain, alpine scenery, and rich cultural history, particularly in music. Austria has a temperate climate, with cold winters and mild summers. Its geography is dominated by the Alps. It is known for its imperial history and as the birthplace of many famous composers. Aliases: Republic of Austria.

The People's Republic of Bangladesh is a country in South Asia, located at the mouth of the Ganges and Brahmaputra rivers. It is a densely populated country with a fertile deltaic plain landscape. Bangladesh has a humid subtropical climate. Its history is marked by its emergence as an independent nation in 1971. It is a major producer of rice and jute. Aliases: People's Republic of Bangladesh.

The Kingdom of Belgium is a country in Western Europe, known for its medieval towns, Renaissance architecture, and as the headquarters of the European Union. It has a temperate maritime climate and diverse geography, including coastal plains and rolling hills. Belgium has a complex linguistic and cultural landscape, with Dutch, French, and German as official languages. Aliases: Kingdom of Belgium.

The Federative Republic of Brazil is the largest country in both South America and Latin America. It is the world's fifth-largest country by area and the seventh most populous. Brazil is a federal republic known for its vibrant culture, diverse population, and vast natural resources, including the Amazon rainforest. Its geography is characterized by rainforests, savannas, and a long Atlantic coastline. The climate is predominantly tropical. Aliases: Federative Republic of Brazil.

Canada is a country in the northern part of North America. It is the world's second-largest country by total area. Canada is a parliamentary democracy and a constitutional monarchy, known for its multiculturalism and vast, diverse landscapes, including mountains, forests, and tundra. Its climate varies from temperate in the south to arctic in the north. Canada is rich in natural resources and has a highly developed economy.

The Republic of Chile is a long, narrow country occupying a strip of land between the Andes to the east and the Pacific Ocean to the west. It is known for its diverse geography, ranging from the driest desert in the world (Atacama) to alpine tundras and glaciers in the south. Chile has a varied climate due to its length. It is a republic with a rich cultural heritage. Aliases: Republic of Chile.

The People's Republic of China is a sovereign state in East Asia, the world's most populous country. It is a single-party socialist republic governed by the Communist Party. China boasts a rich and ancient history, with significant contributions to philosophy, science, and art. Its economy has experienced rapid growth, making it a major global economic force. The landscape is incredibly diverse, from the Gobi Desert to the Himalayan mountains and fertile river valleys. Aliases: People's Republic of China; PRC.

The Republic of Colombia is a country in the northwestern part of South America. It is known for its diverse geography, including the Andes mountains, Amazon rainforest, and Caribbean and Pacific coastlines. Colombia is one of the most biodiverse countries in the world. It has a rich cultural heritage influenced by indigenous, Spanish, and African traditions. The climate varies from tropical along the coasts to alpine in the mountains. Aliases: Republic of Colombia.

The Kingdom of Denmark is a country in Northern Europe, located southwest of Sweden and south of Norway. It is known for its flat landscape, extensive coastline, and contribution to Scandinavian design and culture ('hygge'). Denmark has a temperate maritime climate. It is a constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary democracy. Aliases: Kingdom of Denmark.

The Arab Republic of Egypt is a transcontinental country spanning the northeast corner of Africa and southwest corner of Asia, via a land bridge formed by the Sinai Peninsula. Egypt is renowned for its ancient civilization, pyramids, and pharaonic history. Its geography is dominated by the Nile River valley and delta, surrounded by desert. The climate is hot and arid. Egypt is a significant cultural and political center in the Arab world. Aliases: Arab Republic of Egypt.

The Republic of Finland is a country in Northern Europe. It is known for its vast forests, numerous lakes, and its sauna culture. Finland has a cold continental climate, with cold winters and warm summers. It is a constitutional republic and a member of the European Union. It is also known for its technological innovation and high quality of life. Aliases: Republic of Finland.

The French Republic is a country primarily located in Western Europe, consisting of metropolitan France and several overseas regions and territories. France is a unitary semi-presidential republic known for its rich history, culture, art, and cuisine. Its diverse geography includes plains, forests, mountains (Alps, Pyrenees), and a long coastline. The climate is largely temperate, with Mediterranean influences in the south. It is a major player in international affairs. Aliases: French Republic.

The Federal Republic of Germany is a central European country. It is a federal parliamentary republic and a major economic power within Europe and the world. Germany has a long and influential history, playing a central role in European events. Its landscape includes forests, plains, and the Alps in the south, with a temperate seasonal climate. It is known for its engineering, automotive industry, and rich cultural heritage. Aliases: Federal Republic of Germany.

The Hellenic Republic, commonly known as Greece, is a country in Southeastern Europe. It is the birthplace of democracy, Western philosophy, and classical antiquity. Greece has a vast coastline and numerous islands, with a Mediterranean climate. Its geography includes mountains and coastal plains. It is a popular tourist destination and a member of the European Union. Aliases: Hellenic Republic.

The Republic of India is a country in South Asia. It is the world's seventh-largest country by area, the second-most populous country, and the most populous democracy in the world. India is characterized by its immense diversity in culture, language, and religion. Its history spans millennia, with numerous empires and dynasties shaping its heritage. The geography varies from the Himalayan mountains in the north to the tropical southern coasts. Aliases: Republic of India.

The Republic of Indonesia is a country in Southeast Asia and Oceania, consisting of over 17,000 islands. It is the world's largest island country and the fourth most populous. Indonesia is known for its diverse cultures, languages, and rich biodiversity. Its geography is volcanic and tropical, with a tropical rainforest climate. It is a major producer of commodities like palm oil and coal. Aliases: Republic of Indonesia.

The Islamic Republic of Iran, also known as Persia, is a country in Western Asia. It is known for its rich history, Persian culture, and significant oil and gas reserves. Iran's geography is diverse, featuring mountains, deserts, and a coastline along the Persian Gulf and Caspian Sea. The climate ranges from arid to subtropical. Iran has been a major geopolitical player for millennia. Aliases: Islamic Republic of Iran.

The Republic of Ireland is an island country in the North Atlantic, west of Great Britain. It is known for its green landscapes, rugged cliffs, and rich cultural heritage, including Celtic traditions and literature. Ireland has a temperate maritime climate, characterized by mild, wet winters and cool summers. It is a member of the European Union. Aliases: Republic of Ireland.

The Italian Republic is a country consisting of a peninsula delimited by the Alps and surrounded by the Mediterranean Sea. Italy has a rich history, being the birthplace of Roman civilization and the Renaissance. It is known for its art, culture, fashion, and cuisine. Its geography includes mountains, plains, and extensive coastlines, with a Mediterranean climate. Italy is a founding member of the European Union and a major global economy. Aliases: Italian Republic.

Japan is an island country in East Asia, located in the northwest Pacific Ocean. It is a constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary government. Japan is known for its unique culture, technological advancements, and rich history, often blending ancient traditions with modernity. The geography is mountainous and volcanic, with a temperate climate. Despite its limited land resources, it is a major global economic power. Aliases: Nihon; Nippon.

Malaysia is a country in Southeast Asia, consisting of thirteen states and three federal territories. It is separated by the South China Sea into two regions: Peninsular Malaysia and Malaysian Borneo. Malaysia is known for its multicultural population, diverse geography including rainforests and coastlines, and a tropical climate. It has a developing economy with significant manufacturing and resource sectors.

The United Mexican States, commonly known as Mexico, is a country in the southern portion of North America. It is a federal republic comprising 31 states and Mexico City. Mexico has a rich pre-Columbian history and a vibrant culture influenced by indigenous and Spanish traditions. Its geography is diverse, featuring mountains, deserts, and tropical coastlines. The climate ranges from arid to tropical. Aliases: United Mexican States.

The Kingdom of the Netherlands is a densely populated country located mostly in Western Europe. It is known for its low-lying geography, extensive canal systems, and windmills. The Netherlands has a rich history of trade and exploration, and is a major international hub. Its landscape is largely flat and reclaimed from the sea. The climate is temperate maritime. Aliases: Kingdom of the Netherlands.

New Zealand is an island country in the southwestern Pacific Ocean. It is known for its dramatic landscapes, including mountains, fjords, glaciers, and beaches, as well as its unique wildlife, such as the kiwi bird. New Zealand has a temperate climate. Its culture is a blend of Māori and European influences. It is a constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary democracy.

The Federal Republic of Nigeria is a country in West Africa. It is the most populous country in Africa and the seventh most populous country in the world. Nigeria is a federal republic with a diverse landscape, including savannas, rainforests, and a long coastline. Its climate is tropical. Nigeria is a major player in African politics and economy, with significant oil reserves. Aliases: Federal Republic of Nigeria.

The Kingdom of Norway is a Nordic country located on the western part of the Scandinavian Peninsula. It is known for its dramatic fjords, mountains, and extensive coastline. Norway has a temperate climate along the coast and a colder continental climate inland. It is a constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary democracy, rich in natural resources like oil and gas. Aliases: Kingdom of Norway.

The Islamic Republic of Pakistan is a country in South Asia. It is the world's fifth-most populous country and has the second-largest Muslim population. Pakistan has a diverse geography, including fertile plains, deserts, and high mountains, including the Karakoram Range. Its history is intertwined with the partition of British India. The climate varies widely across its regions. Aliases: Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

The Republic of Peru is a country in western South America. It is known for its vast archaeological sites, including those of the Inca Empire, its diverse geography spanning the Andes mountains, the Amazon basin, and the Pacific coast. Peru has a varied climate due to its diverse topography. It possesses rich mineral resources and a vibrant cultural heritage. Aliases: Republic of Peru.

The Republic of the Philippines is an archipelago country in Southeast Asia. It consists of about 7,641 islands, divided into three main geographical divisions: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. The Philippines is known for its tropical climate, rich marine biodiversity, and a culture influenced by Spanish and American colonization. Its geography is mountainous and volcanic, with numerous coastlines. Aliases: Republic of the Philippines.

The Republic of Poland is a country in Central Europe. It is a unitary state known for its complex history, including periods of great power and partitions, and its resilience through various conflicts. Poland has a diverse geography, with mountains in the south and plains in the north, and a temperate climate. It is a member of the European Union and NATO, playing a significant role in the region. Aliases: Republic of Poland.

The Portuguese Republic is a country located on the Iberian Peninsula in Southwestern Europe. It is the oldest surviving state on the Iberian Peninsula and one of the oldest nation-states in Europe. Portugal has a long Atlantic coastline, a temperate climate, and a rich history of exploration and maritime trade. Its geography includes plains, mountains, and coastal regions. Aliases: Portuguese Republic.

The Russian Federation is a transcontinental country spanning Eastern Europe and Northern Asia. It is the largest country in the world by area, covering over one-eighth of the Earth's inhabited land area. Russia has a long and complex history, from tsarist rule to Soviet communism and its modern federal republic status. Its vast landscape includes plains, forests, tundra, and mountains, with a predominantly continental climate. Russia possesses immense natural resources. Aliases: Russian Federation.

The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is a country in Western Asia, constituting the bulk of the Arabian Peninsula. It is a sovereign Arab and Islamic state known for its vast oil reserves and role in the Islamic world as the custodian of Mecca and Medina. Its geography is predominantly desert, with a hot and arid climate. Saudi Arabia has a significant geopolitical influence due to its energy resources and religious importance. Aliases: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

The Republic of South Africa is the southernmost country in Africa. It is known for its diverse landscapes, including savannas, deserts, and mountains, and its rich biodiversity. South Africa has a complex history, including apartheid, and is now a democratic republic with a multicultural society. Its climate varies from Mediterranean in the southwest to temperate and subtropical. It is a major economic power on the continent. Aliases: Republic of South Africa.

The Republic of Korea, commonly known as South Korea, is a country in the western part of East Asia. It is a democratic republic with a highly developed economy, known for its technological advancements and vibrant popular culture (K-pop, K-drama). South Korea has a complex history, marked by division and rapid post-war development. The geography is predominantly mountainous, with a temperate climate. It is a major global economic and cultural force. Aliases: Republic of Korea.

The Kingdom of Spain is a country in Southwestern Europe, occupying the majority of the Iberian Peninsula. It is a constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system. Spain has a rich and diverse history, influenced by Roman, Moorish, and Christian cultures, reflected in its art, architecture, and festivals. Its geography includes mountains, plateaus, and extensive coastlines, with a predominantly Mediterranean climate. It is known for its vibrant culture and significant tourism industry. Aliases: Kingdom of Spain.

The Kingdom of Sweden is a Nordic country in Northern Europe. It is known for its extensive forests, numerous lakes, and a long coastline. Sweden is a constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary democracy, recognized for its high standard of living, social welfare system, and minimalist design. Its geography includes vast forests and mountains in the west. The climate is temperate, with cold winters and mild summers. Aliases: Kingdom of Sweden.

The Swiss Confederation, commonly known as Switzerland, is a federal republic in Central Europe. It is known for its stunning alpine scenery, neutrality, banking sector, and direct democracy. Switzerland has a temperate climate with significant variations due to altitude. Its geography is dominated by the Alps, Jura mountains, and the Swiss Plateau. It has four national languages: German, French, Italian, and Romansh. Aliases: Swiss Confederation.

The Kingdom of Thailand is a country in Southeast Asia. It is a constitutional monarchy known for its tropical beaches, ornate royal palaces, and ancient ruins. Thailand has a rich history and a vibrant culture, heavily influenced by Buddhism. Its geography includes mountains in the north, a plateau in the northeast, and a long coastline. The climate is tropical monsoon. Aliases: Kingdom of Thailand.

The Republic of Turkey is a transcontinental country located mainly on the Anatolian Peninsula in Western Asia, with a smaller portion on the Balkan Peninsula in Southeastern Europe. Turkey has a rich history, bridging Eastern and Western civilizations, and was the seat of the Ottoman Empire. Its geography is diverse, including mountains, plateaus, and coastlines along the Mediterranean and Black Seas. The climate varies from Mediterranean to continental. Aliases: Republic of Turkey.

The United Kingdom is a sovereign country in northwestern Europe, consisting of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. It is a constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary democracy. The UK has a vast global history, including a colonial empire that once spanned the globe. Its geography includes varied landscapes from highlands to plains, with a temperate maritime climate. It is a significant cultural and financial center. Aliases: UK; Great Britain.

The United States of America is a federal republic consisting of 50 states, a federal district, and numerous territories. It is a global superpower with significant economic, political, and cultural influence. Its diverse geography ranges from temperate forests and plains to deserts and mountains, with a varied climate across its vast expanse. The nation's history is marked by westward expansion, industrialization, and its role in major global conflicts. Aliases: USA; America.

The Socialist Republic of Vietnam is the easternmost country on the Indochinese Peninsula. It is known for its long coastline, tropical climate, and rich history, including its struggle for independence. Vietnam's geography ranges from mountainous interiors to fertile deltas. It is a major producer of rice and coffee, and its economy has grown rapidly in recent decades. Aliases: Socialist Republic of Vietnam.

Any perceived connection is purely coincidental, as the two distinct surnames share a phonetic similarity despite having entirely different etymologies. 3. While the name "Muhammad" has only one standard spelling in Arabic, its English transliteration allows for various spellings (e.g., "Mohammed," "Muhamad," "Mohamed," "Mohammad," or "Muhammed"). These variations are merely linguistic translations and are all equally valid for character naming. 4. Russian names ending in "-y" (e.g., "Dmitry") are often transliterated into English using "-i" (e.g., "Dmitri"), and vice versa. Both versions are acceptable and serve as valid character names. 5. "Sean," "Shaun," and "Shawn" are variations of the same name. "Sean" adheres more closely to its original Gaelic roots, while "Shaun" and "Shawn" are anglicized versions; all three are equally suitable for naming characters. 6. Surnames of Gaelic origin starting with "Mc" (e.g., "McCallum") can also be written with "Mac" (e.g., "MacCallum") and vice versa. Both spellings are valid linguistic variations of the same name. 7. "John" and "Jonathan" are distinct and separate names. 8. After World War Two, the German name "Adolf" became taboo and pretty much went extinct. Many Indonesians (especially Javanese) simply do not have a surname, but it varies from one ethnic group to another. 6. Ethiopians don't have surnames. They have a first name and then their father's name (and also optional grandfather's name after father's name). It means that the second and optional third name aren't fixed and are changing with each new generation of the same family. It also means that wives don't take their husbands' "surname" since it's not even a surname to begin with. 7. Chinese, Japanese, Hungarians, Koreans and Vietnamese place their surnames first. 8. Mixed heritages are a thing. 9. Double surnames are common in Spanish and Portuguese naming customs. First part of a double surname is from father (his first surname specifically if he has two) and a second part is from mother (her first surname specifically if she has two as well). In formal context, both surnames are used as a single entity. And in informal contexts, a person may be referred by a father's part of their double surname only. Portuguese surnames follow the exact same rules except mother's surname is written first. Both Spanish and Portuguese double surnames are space-separated without hyphens. 10. In Spanish and Portuguese, it's common to have a first name comprised from two first names. It's not the same thing as English middle names since both Spanish/Portuguese first names are officially used as a single entity. Although, in informal contexts, only the first first name is used. Double first names are also a thing in French, although hyphenated. There's no specific rules for amount of names and surnames for Spanish/Portugese-speaking people, so it can be; One first name and one surname, two first names and one surname, one first name and two surnames, or two first names and two surnames per person. 11. In Russian, there's such thing as "patronymics". It's the father's name that's placed between first and last names (just like a middle name in English). Do not mistake patronymics as a middle or a second first name, they're a whole different thing. Patronymics are gendered. There's 2 things that affect patronymic's ending: descendant's gender and whenever their father's name ends with vowel or consonant. Male and vowel: -evich Male and consonant: -ovich Female and vowel: -evna Female and consonant: -ovna Here's some examples: For example: Sergey has two kids, the son is "Sergeyevich" and the daughter is "Sergeyevna". Oleg has two kids as well, the son is "Olegovich" and the daughter is "Olegovna". Certain names are unique exceptions that define patronymic's ending: Childern of Lev are "Lvovich" and "Lvovna". Children of Foma are "Fomich" and "Fominichna". Children of Ilya are "Ilyich" and "Ilyinichna". Children of Kuzma are "Kuzmich" and "Kuzminichna". Children of Pavel are "Pavlovich" and "Pavlovna". Children of Nikita are "Nikitich" and "Nikitichna". If a Russian person has a child in a country that doesn't use patronymics, then it's not added to official documents. Do not mistake patronymics with surnames derived from first names (e.g. "Antonov" and "Antonova" are surnames while "Antonovich" and "Antonovna" are patronymics). And yes, it also applies to those of a mixed heritage. So if a foreigner decides to have kids in a country that uses patronymics then their name will be used as a base for patronymics following the exact same rules. So, kids of a hypothetical Englishman named "Harold" Will be "Haroldovich" and "Haroldovna". Patronymics also exist in Bulgarian language, although they lack unique suffixes like in Russian and instead use the same suffixes as surnames, so "Borisov", "Ivanov" and others can be both surnames and patronymics in Bulgarian without any changes. 12. Surname Law has been adopted Turkey on 21 June 1934, so no official surnames for everyone who died before that date. Prior to this date, however, Turkish families in the major urban centres had unofficial names by which they were known locally (often ending with the suffixes -zade, -oğlu or -gil), and were used in similar manner to a surname. 13. Names from different Germanic countries are often interchangeable. 14. Gendered Surnames are a thing in some languages: In Russian, Female versions of surnames that end with "-ov", "-ev", and "-in" should also feature "-a" after them, So the daughters of Chernov, Zvyagintsev and Malinin would be Chernova, Zvyagintseva and Malinina respectively. Surnames that end with "-y" should end with "-aya" instead, but it also depends wherever the letter before "-y" is a vowel or consonant. If the letter before "-y" is a vowel then the "-aya" replaces both last letters, so the daughter of Donskoy would be Donskaya, but if the letter before "-y" is a consonant then "-aya" replaces this last letter only, so the daughter of Sokolovsky would be Sokolovskaya. In Polish, surnames that end with "-ski" and "-zki" have "-a" replacing the "-i", so a daughter of Bobrowski will be Bobrowska. In Bulgarian, it's the same pattern as in Russian, but surnames that end with "-ski" specifically shall end with "-ska" instead. In Latvian, If a surname ends with "-s" and the letter before it is a vowel, then the female version will end with "-e", replacing both "-s" and the said vowel, so the daughter of Zvirbulis would be Zvirbule. And if a surname ends with "-s" with a consonant before it, then the female version will end with "-a", replacing only "-s", so the daughter of Kalniņš would be Kalniņa. The exception from this rule is if the said consonant before "-s" is "k", in which case, female version will end in "-ce", replacing both last letters, so the daughter of Skujenieks would be Skujeniece. In Lithuanian, female suffix for surnames is different depending on if a woman is married or not. For married women the suffix is "-ienė", but there are different suffixes for unmarried women: "-as": "-itė" for unmarried. "-ys": "-ytė" for unmarried. "-us": "-utė" for unmarried. "-is": "-yte" for unmarried. Married suffix replaces the entire male suffix, so a wife of Jankauskas will be Jankauskienė, while unmarried suffix only takes the "-s" from a male suffix, so a daugther of Jankauskas will be Jankauskaitė. The exception to this rules are surnames that end with "-is", whereby unmarried suffix replaces the entire male suffix just like married one would, so a daughter of Balaišis will be Balaišytė. Lithuanian woman retains married suffix even if she becomes a widow. 15. Icelanders do not have surnames. Instead, they have a first name followed by either a patronymic or a matronymic, which is their parent's name that ends with "-son" if the descendant a boy, "-dóttir" if the descendant is a girl and, since 2019, a gender-neutral "-bur". Since there's a choice between father's and mother's name, siblings can have different "surnames". 16. Norwegian surnames were originally patronymic until a law was passed in 1923 which had ordered that all newborn children should be assigned a hereditary family name at birth. Same thing with Sweden, except their law was passed in 1901.
